description: Mixes several files under a moving-fader automation score: balance_data lists, per timepoint, the RELATIVE level of every file (each line is auto-SCALED to sum to 1 - verified: a '2 3' line renders byte-identical to '0.4 0.6'), and envelope_data shapes the OVERALL loudness of the summed mix over time. The relative mix is therefore always a convex combination (cannot overload by itself), but the overall envelope CAN push it over full scale - and then the 16-bit output WRAPS (verified: envelope 3.0 on hot material, 100% of over-samples bit-match wrap_int16, 0% match clipping - the P5-3 pathology). Output duration = the LONGEST input, exact on all probes (2.0 both orders; 3.0 with three files). Cross-validated against the family: a linear 1->0 balance under a flat envelope renders BYTE-IDENTICAL to submix crossfade mode 1 on the same pair. This entry pins TWO inputs (a 3-file run verified - execute() for more; balance lines then need one level column per file). All files must share one channel count (refusal verbatim). Deterministic.
musical_use: Level automation as a score: ride two layers against each other with arbitrary trajectories - slow figure/ground swaps, rhythmic ducking, a texture that surfaces only in the gaps of another - then master the whole gesture with one overall envelope (swells, fades, pulses). This is the multi-file generalisation of submix balance's single fader, and the mixfile stage is bypassed entirely: write both data files with write_data_file() and go straight to sound. Times in both files are output-time seconds; values between timepoints interpolate linearly. Keep the envelope at or below 1 unless you KNOW the summed material has headroom - overs WRAP, they do not saturate (stage headroom in the sources or the envelope, never after). The balance file cannot vary the overall level (lines are re-scaled to sum 1) - that is exactly what envelope_data is for.

balance_data.description: REQUIRED text file of fader positions (write with write_data_file()): each line = a time followed by ONE relative level per input file, in argv order ('0 1 0' then '1 0 1' crossfades file1 -> file2 over a second). Lines are auto-scaled to sum to 1 (verified byte-identical for '2 3' vs '0.4 0.6'), so only RATIOS matter. Data must begin at time zero ('ERROR: Data in datafile <name> must begin at time zero' - verified) and times must increase. A line of all zeros refuses 'ERROR: levels are zero at line N' (N counts one PAST the last line on a single-line file - off-by-one, verbatim). Wrong column count refuses with a MISLEADING 'Times 0.000000 and 0.000000 too close in datafile <name>' (the parser reads the extra number as the next time). Renders in the argv after the output, before envelope_data.

envelope_data.description: REQUIRED overall-loudness envelope for the summed mix: time/value pairs ('0 1' newline '2 1' = flat unity for 2 s). Values are CDP-enforced 0-256 per point ('Value (9000.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 256.000000) in brkpntfile <name>' - verbatim), and anything driving the sum past full scale WRAPS (see known_issues). A flat 0.5 envelope renders exactly 0.5x the flat-1.0 render (verified to 1 LSB). CDP also accepts a bare scalar in this argv slot (verified: '0.5' == the 0.5x render) - this entry pins the file form; write a two-line flat file for constants.

examples.description: Slow figure/ground swap between two textures with a gentle master fade-out.
examples.expected_use:
write_data_file('bal.txt', '0 1 0.2
4 0.2 1
8 1 0.2') and write_data_file('env.txt', '0 1
7 1
8 0'). input = [textureA, textureB]; output lasts as long as the longer input.

examples.description: Flat equal mix at safe level (constant envelope as a 2-line file).
examples.expected_use: eq.txt = '0 1 1' (scaled to 0.5/0.5); flat.txt = '0 0.9\n30 0.9' (times may exceed the mix length harmlessly).

known_issues: OVERLOAD WRAPS (same pathology as submix mix, P5-3): when envelope x mix exceeds full scale, the output equals INTEGER WRAPAROUND of the ideal sum (verified: envelope 3.0 on near-full-scale material - every over-sample bit-matches wrap_int16, none match clipping; positive overs return as large negative samples). The balance stage cannot overload (convex), so the envelope is the only risky knob: keep it <= 1 unless the sources have measured headroom. getlevel cannot pre-flight this mode (no mixfile) - stage headroom in the sources or envelope.

NO SAMPLE-RATE VALIDATION (first-class divergence): a 44.1 kHz + 22.05 kHz pair is ACCEPTED (exit 0) and the mismatched file is read at the output rate - double-speed chipmunking, no warning. Every other probed submix mode refuses mixed rates. Verify rates yourself before calling.

Channel counts must match: 'ERROR: Process only works with files having the same number of channels: file N will not work' (verbatim). Stereo pairs verified clean. Single input refused ('Insufficient input files for this process').
balance_data lines are re-scaled to sum to 1 - the file CANNOT change the overall level (banner-documented, byte-verified). Use envelope_data for level moves.
This entry pins 2 inputs; the binary is variadic (3-file run verified, balance lines carrying 3 columns). Use execute() for wider stacks.

Data-file refusals are quoted verbatim in the parameter descriptions (begin-at-zero, zero-levels with its off-by-one line number, the misleading wrong-column-count message). Envelope point values cap at 256.
Deterministic: identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart. Cross-check: linear balance + flat envelope == submix crossfade 1, byte-identical (recorded in the tranche transcript).
Multi-input entry: duration rule (indur_max) verified at 2 and 3 inputs; duration_row null (tranche-11 rule; aux files also don't fit the shared fixture).
